questions.question: What is the difference between & and && in C?
questions.solution_html:
• - `&` is a bitwise AND operator, performing binary operations on integers.
  • - `&&` is a logical AND operator, used for conditional statements, evaluating true or false.
  • Example
  • int x = 5; // binary: 101
  • int y = 3; // binary: 011
  • int result1 = x & y; // bitwise and: 001 (1 in decimal)
  • int result2 = (x > 0) && (y > 0); // logical and: true (1 in decimal)
